u_cam_ml_02_classifier_2026_04_21.description: Follow-up surfaced by U-CAM-ML-05 LoRA training result. Hypothesis: .MIN files misclassified by extension (okuma_native) when JM Die uses hyperMILL â†’ Okuma post. Fix: header-based override in CAMFeatureExtractorEngine.inferCAMSystemFromHeader â€” detects MASTERCAM / HYPERMILL / FUSION 360 / INVENTOR HSM / SOLIDCAM / OPEN MIND banners in the first 4KB and overrides the extension-based cam_system with confidence='header_match' and an evidence string.
u_cam_ml_02_classifier_2026_04_21.empirical_finding: Scanned 500 .MIN files from the corpus â€” ZERO contained CAM signatures in their first 4KB. JM Die's Okuma lathe corpus is genuinely Okuma-native ($filename.MIN% header + NAT op markers + direct T/S/F codes, no CAM banner). The extension-based classification IS correct for this corpus. The hypothesis that motivated U-CAM-ML-05 skipping all 8 slots was wrong â€” the real issue is that JM Die's lathe archive has no Mastercam/hyperMILL-branded programs, not that we were misreading them.
